overview: Training and development managers plan how an organization builds its people's skills. They analyze training needs, design programs, manage budgets and instructors, and measure whether training works. O*NET rates knowledge of education and training at 4.93 out of 5 for this job and learning strategies at 4.25. Most hold a bachelor's degree, 71% in O*NET data, and 21% a master's degree, often in HR, education or organizational psychology. The BLS May 2025 median is $133,000 across 48,050 jobs. The role mixes desk work with leading people and presenting to leaders.
pay: Training and development managers earn a median of $133,000, and the top 10% earn $233,600 or more. Delaware has the highest state median at $172,340, 30% above the national figure, with New York close behind at $171,400. California has the most jobs, 6,680, at a median of $156,260.

faq.q: How much do training and development managers make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $133,000 a year. The middle half earn between $101,850 and $176,870. Delaware, New York and Washington ($163,360) have the highest state medians, while Montana ($98,950) and Mississippi ($88,030) pay the least. Large companies usually pay more than small ones.

faq.q: What degree do you need for training and development?
faq.a: Most managers hold a bachelor's degree, 71% in O*NET data, and 21% a master's degree. There are 9 related majors, including adult education, learning sciences and industrial and organizational psychology. Several years as a trainer or HR specialist usually come first.

faq.q: What skills do training managers need?
faq.a: O*NET rates learning strategies at 4.25 out of 5 for this job, and speaking, reading comprehension and active listening at 4. Knowledge of personnel and human resources is rated 3.96. You need to plan programs, coach instructors and show results with data.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to training and development manager?
faq.a: The closest moves are Medical and Health Services Managers (85% match), Project Management Specialists (82%) and Industrial-Organizational Psychologists (81%). I-O psychologists earn $193,950, 46% more, according to BLS May 2025, but usually need a graduate degree. Sales Managers are an 80% match and earn $148,270.
